## The symptom

`:3070` (the operator that serves every page over SSE/sync) goes **"connection refused on all pages"** in recurring windows — the client shows **"Operator connection lost"** then reconnects ("Welcome back, User"), sometimes seconds apart, for anywhere from ~1 to ~35 minutes, then self-recovers. The operator journal during a window:

```
[hono-host] fatal unhandledRejection — exiting: Error: Cannot find module
  '.../papercusp-release/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/cjs/types.js'  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
[cluster] worker N exited (code=1 signal=null); respawn budget exhausted (160) — NOT respawning
[cluster] SIGTERM — draining 32 worker(s) + exiting primary
```

`NRestarts=0` at the systemd level can hide it — the storm is the **cluster primary respawning workers**, not systemd restarting the service.

## The mechanism (root cause)

`:3070` runs the `papercusp-release` checkout. A deploy shells `setup-release-checkout.sh`, whose step 3 historically refreshed node_modules **in place**:

```sh
[ -e "$dest" ] && rm -rf "$dest"      # deletes the LIVE root node_modules
cp -al "$nm" "$dest"                  # then slowly (~a minute, 100k+ files) re-hardlinks it
```

This tree "never `npm install`s" — it **hardlink-copies** node_modules from the integration tree. For the whole ~minute the root `cp -al` runs, the live operator's node_modules is **deleted or half-populated**. Any worker that (re)boots in that window — a `lag-self-restart`, a crash respawn, a deploy restart racing the copy — `require()`s a module that isn't there yet → `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` → it exits → the primary respawns it → it crashes again → **the 160-respawn budget (workers×5 = 32×5) burns out → 0 live workers → connection refused on every page**. When the copy finishes the next restart boots clean and it self-recovers — which is why it looks transient and recurs on (dep-changing) deploys.

`PAPERCUSP_CLUSTER=32` maximizes the blast radius: one inconsistent tree crash-loops all 32 workers at once.

## The fix — four layers

**1. Atomic node_modules swap (root cause removal)** — `setup-release-checkout.sh` `sync_one_node_modules()`. Hardlink-copy into a **sibling** temp (`$dest.deploy-tmp.$$`, same depth so the workspace packages' relative `../../packages/X` symlinks resolve identically), then swap with **two fast renames** (`mv dest old; mv tmp dest; rm old`). The live tree is only ever **complete**; the exposure shrinks from ~a minute to the microseconds between two `rename(2)`s. `set -e` aborts a failed `cp` *before* any swap, so a partial copy can never replace the live tree.

**2. Workspace-resolution gate — step 3c (EI-2118)** — `setup-release-checkout.sh` step 3c. A related but distinct failure mode: the `need_node_modules()` heuristic compares entry **names** via `ls`+`diff`, which cannot detect a dangling symlink (it exists by name but the target is absent). Before EI-2118, a dangling `@papercusp/<pkg>` symlink in the release tree slipped through that check, the deploy skipped the re-copy, and the operator crash-looped on `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` at the restart cutover (2026-06-20 `@papercusp/plugin-loader`). The fix: `unresolved_workspace_pkgs()` walks `@papercusp`/`@papercup` in both trees using `-e` (which **follows** symlinks), so a dangling link fails the test. `need_node_modules()` in `auto` mode now also calls it and forces a re-copy when any package is unresolved. After the copy, step 3c runs `unresolved_workspace_pkgs()` once more: if any package still doesn't resolve, the script **exits 1 before any restart** — the old process keeps serving, zero downtime.

**3. Boot-integrity preflight (fail fast + named)** — `boot-integrity-preflight.ts`, run as the **first import** of `hono-host.ts` via `boot-integrity-first.ts` (so it evaluates before the heavy import graph). It `require.resolve`s a manifest of load-bearing modules; on a broken/partial tree it logs one **named** diagnostic and exits `78` (distinct, `EX_CONFIG`) instead of a deep `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` stack. The module is **dependency-free** (only `node:module`) so it can't be a victim of the inconsistency it checks. Manifest entries are **resolve-verified against a healthy tree** — naïve `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `mem0ai/package.json` FAIL even when installed (exports-map quirks), so the manifest uses the forms that actually resolve.

**4. Cluster boot-failure backstop (no respawn storm)** — `cluster-fork.ts`, opt-in via `onUnbootable`. A worker that exits within `bootGraceMs` (10s) of fork never came up; if a **whole generation** fails that way and **none was ever healthy**, the build is unbootable → halt the respawn storm and call `onUnbootable` (→ exit the primary clean/fast/distinct so the supervisor/deploy rolls back) instead of burning all 160 respawns. A worker that crashes **after** surpassing the grace window is a normal runtime crash and still respawns — `onUnbootable` never fires once any worker has been healthy.

Layers 1–2 prevent inconsistent trees from reaching the live operator (either by making the swap atomic or by aborting before cutover); layers 3–4 turn any *remaining* inconsistency (a botched rollback, a non-manifest module) into a fast, loud, self-correcting fail instead of an hour-long all-pages outage.

## Diagnosing / recovering a live incident

- `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3070/api/health` → `000`/connection-refused = down; the journal grep above confirms the MODULE_NOT_FOUND crash-loop.
- It usually **self-recovers** once the in-place copy finishes; if wedged, the documented recovery is `systemctl --user stop papercup-dev-api.service` then re-run the deploy (`PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DEV_RESTART=1 npx tsx apps/operator/lib/release/deploy-cli.ts --execute --no-drain`) or `npm ci` in `papercusp-release` to complete node_modules.
- Confirm `papercusp-release/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/cjs/types.js` and `@papercusp/plugin-loader` resolve (`cd papercusp-release && node -e "require.resolve('@papercusp/plugin-loader')"`).
